x: God Almighty means by His saying,
, that is, when the shout of the Resurrection descends, which is when the Trumpet is blown for the establishment of the Hour.
It was also narrated on the authority of Al-Hussein, who said: I heard Abu Muadh say:

c: Ubaid told us:
m: I heard Al-Dahhak say regarding His statement,
h
When the Event occurs
, meaning: the shout.

c: Ali told us: Abu Saleh told us: Muawiyah told us, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: regarding his statement,
h
When the Event occurs
, the Event, the Calamity, the Deafening Scream, and similar names of the Resurrection. God has made it great and warned His servants about it.

x: , God Almighty says: The occurrence of the event is not false, nor can it be rejected, nor can it be dual. And false in this context is a source like consequence and well-being. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.

c: Bishr told us: Yazid told us: Saeed told us on the authority of Qatada:
m: h
Its occurrence is not false
: meaning it has no duality, no return, and no reversal.

c: Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Ibn Thawr told us on the authority of Muammar on the authority of Qatada
m: regarding his statement,
h
Its occurrence is not false
, he said: It is dual.
b.via: Muammar on the authority of Qatada

x: And His saying, lowering and raising, God Almighty says: The event will then lower people who were dear to God’s fire in this world. His saying, lowering and raising, means: It raised people who were lowly in this world to the mercy of God and His Paradise. It was also said: It lowered, so that the nearest could hear, and it raised, so that the farthest could hear.

c: Ibn Hamid told us: Yahya bin Wadh told us:
m: Ubaidullah, meaning Al-Ataki, told us on the authority of Uthman bin Abdullah bin Saraqa: A lowering and raising one: He said: The Hour will lower the enemies of God to Hell and raise the friends of God to Paradise.

c: Bishr told us: Yazid told us: Saeed told us on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement, lowering and raising, meaning: It penetrated every plain and mountain until it made everyone, near and far, hear. Then it raised some people to the honor of God and lowered some people to the punishment of God.

c: Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Ibn Thaur told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada,
m: lowering and raising. He said: I made the near and the far hear, lowering some people to the punishment of God and raising some people to the honor of God.

c: Ibn Hamid told us: Yahya bin Wadh told us: Al-Hasan told us, on the authority of Yazid, on the authority of Ikrimah,
m: regarding his statement, lowering and raising, he said: It lowered and made the nearest hear, and it raised and made the farthest hear. He said: So the near and the far from God were equal.

c: Muhammad bin Saad told me: My father told me: My uncle told me: My father told me on the authority of his father on the authority of Ibn Abbas:
m: Lowering and Raising. He said: I heard it from near and far.
b.via: his father on the authority of Ibn Abbas

c: It was narrated on the authority of Al-Hussein,
m: who said: I heard Abu Muadh saying: Ubaid narrated to us, who said: I heard Al-Dahhak say regarding His statement, lowering and raising, that it lowered so that the nearest could be heard, and it raised so that the farthest could be heard, so the near and the far were equal in it.

x: When the earth is shaken with a violent shaking

, God Almighty says: When the earth is shaken and moved with a movement, from their saying, The arrow shakes in the target, meaning: it shakes and trembles. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.

m: Ali told me: Abu Saleh told us: Asim told us: Isa told us.

c: Al-Harith told me: Al-Hasan told us: Warqa’ told us,
m: both on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement,
h
When the earth is shaken with a violent shaking
, he said: It is shaken.

c: Bishr told us: Yazid told us: Saeed told us on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement,
h
When the earth is shaken with a mighty shaking
, meaning: shaken with a severe earthquake.

c: Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Ibn Thaur told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada:
m: h
When the earth is shaken with a violent shaking
, meaning: It is shaken with an earthquake.

x: And the mountains will be crushed to dust

, God Almighty says: The mountains will be crushed to dust and will become like powdered flour, which is wet, as God Almighty said: And the mountains will become a heap of sand. Al-Muzzammil 14. Basisa, among the Arabs, means flour and gruel that has been crushed and made into provisions. It was mentioned about a thief from Ghatafan that he wanted to bake bread, but he was afraid that he would hurry up and eat the bread before the flour was ready, and he said, Do not bake bread and bake it in batches. Smooth with the smoothness of the Al-Halsi sheep And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.

c: Ali told me: Abu Saleh told us: Muawiyah told us, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: regarding his statement,
h
And the mountains will be crushed to dust
, meaning: they will be shattered to dust.

c: Al-Harith told me: Al-Hasan told us: Warqa’ told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: regarding his statement,
h
And the mountains will be crushed to dust
, he said: They will be shattered.

c: Ibn Bashar told us: Abd al-Rahman told us: Sufyan told us, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: regarding his statement,
h
And the mountains will be dried up completely
, he said: Just as gruel dries up.

c: Ahmad bin Amr Al-Basri told me: Hafs bin Omar Al-Adani told us, on the authority of Al-Hakam bin Aban, on the authority of Ikrimah:
m: And the mountains were crushed to dust. He said: They were shattered to dust.

c: Ismail bin Musa bin Bint Al-Suddi told me: Bishr bin Al-Hakam Al-Ahmasi told us on the authority of Saeed bin Al-Salt on the authority of Ismail Al-Suddi and Abu Saleh:
m: And the mountains were crushed. They said: They were shattered.

c: Ibn Hamid told us: Mihran told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of Mujahid:
m: And the mountains will be dried up. He said: Just as gruel dries up.

c: Yunus told me: Ibn Wahb told us: Ibn Zayd said
m: about the statement of God, And the mountains will be leveled with a complete leveling, that they will become a heap of sand, as God said.

c: Ibn Hamid told us: Jarir told us, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: regarding his statement,
h
And the mountains will be crushed
, he said: They will be shattered.

x: And His saying, And it was scattered dust.
The people of interpretation differed regarding the meaning of dust.
Some of them said: It is the sun’s rays that enter through the window like dust.

c: Ali told me: Abu Saleh told us: Muawiyah told us, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: regarding his statement,
h
Then it became scattered dust
, he said: the rays of the sun.

c: Ibn Hamid told us: Hakam bin Amr told us, on the authority of Ata’, on the authority of Saeed,
m: scattered dust: He said: The sun’s rays when they enter through the window. He said: Jarir narrated to us on the authority of Mansour on the authority of Mujahid regarding his statement, Then it was scattered dust, he said: The sun’s rays enter through the window, but it is nothing.

x: Others said: It is the noise of animals.

c: Ibn Hamid told us: Mihran told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Abu Ishaq, on the authority of Al-Harith, on the authority of Ali,
m: may God be pleased with him, who said: The blaze of beasts.

x: Others said: It is the sparks of fire that fly away without an eye.

c: Muhammad bin Saad told me: My father told me: My uncle told me: My father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: regarding his statement,
h
Then it became scattered dust
. He said: Dust is what flies from the fire when it is blazing, sparks fly from it, but when it falls, it is nothing.

x: Others said: It is the dry tree that is scattered by the wind.

c: Bishr told us: Yazid told us: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement,
h
Then it became scattered dust
, meaning the dust of the trees, blown away by the winds to the right and to the left.

c: Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Ibn Thaur told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement, scattered dust, he said: Dust is what the wind scatters of tree debris. We have explained the meaning of haba in other places with evidence, so there is no need to repeat it here. As for his saying scattered, it means scattered.

x: God Almighty says: You, O people, are of three types and kinds.

c: Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Ibn Thawr told us on the authority of Muammar on the authority of Qatada:
m: And you were three groups. He said: The status of people on the Day of Resurrection.
b.via: Muammar on the authority of Qatada

x: Then the companions of the right - what are the companions of the right

? This is a statement from God about the three pairs. He, the Most High, says: And you were three pairs: the companions of the right, the companions of the left, and the foremost. So He made the report about them sufficient to explain them in the way we mentioned, because the words indicate its meaning. So He said,
Then the companions of the right - what are the companions of the right
? His Prophet Muhammad is amazed by them and said, What are the companions of the right? Al-Waqi’ah 27 Those who will be taken to Paradise by the right, meaning what are the companions of the right?

And the companions of the left, who are the companions of the left? God Almighty says: And the companions of the left are those who will be taken to the left to the Fire. The Arabs call the left hand: the unlucky, and from this is the saying of A'sha of Banu Tha'labah: Then he lowered his evil hands and quenched them with a black branch, thirstier than the branch of the forelock.

, the foremost, they are the third pair, and they are those who were the first to believe in God and His Messenger, and they are the first emigrants. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.

c: Ibn Hamid told us: Yahya bin Wadh told us:
m: Ubaid God, meaning Al-Ataki, told us on the authority of Uthman bin Abdullah bin Saraqa, regarding his statement,
h
And you were three groups
. He said: Two are in Paradise and one is in Hell. He said: The houris are for the forerunners and the Arabs of their age are for the people of Yemen.

c: Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Ibn Thawr told us on the authority of Muammar on the authority of Qatada:
m: h
And you were three groups
. He said: People will remain on the Day of Resurrection.
b.via: Muammar on the authority of Qatada

c: Ibn Bashar told us: Hudha told us: Aouf told us, on the authority of Al-Hasan,
m: regarding His statement, “
h
And you were three groups
. The companions of the right - who are the companions of the right? And the companions of the left - who are the companions of the left?
h
And the foremost

- the foremost - those are the nearest ones” ... to a group of the former peoples * and a few of the latter ones. So the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said, “He made the companions of the right hand of the previous nations equal to the companions of the right hand of this nation.
h
And the foremost
among the nations were more than the foremost among this nation.”

c: Bishr told us: Yazid told us: Saeed told us on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement,
h
Then the companions of the right - what are the companions of the right

?: meaning, what are they for, and what has been prepared for them? And the companions of the left - what are the companions of the left?: meaning, what are they for, and what has been prepared for them?
h
And the foremost
- the foremost?: meaning, from every nation.

c: Yunus told us: Ibn Wahb told us:
m: I heard Ibn Zayd say: I found desire to be of three types. A person makes his desire his knowledge, so his desire prevails over his knowledge, and his desire subdues his knowledge until knowledge with desire is ugly and humiliating, and knowledge is humiliating to desire, and is overwhelming and subduing. So the one who has placed desire and knowledge in his heart, this is one of the people of Hellfire. And if he is one for whom God wants good, he will awaken and become aware, and he will be a helper to knowledge over desire until God makes knowledge prevail over desire. So if the state of the believer improves and his path is straight, then desire will be humiliating and knowledge will be overwhelming and subduing. And if he is one for whom God wants good, he ends his work by making knowledge prevail, so he takes his life, and his knowledge is the dominant one and he is the one who acts upon it, and his desire is humiliating and ugly, and he has no share or action in that. The third: the one whose desire God has made ugly with his knowledge, so his desire does not hope to overcome knowledge or to have half or a share with it. This is the third, and he is the best of you all, and he is the one about whom God, the Exalted, said in Surat al-Waqi’ah 56:And you were three pairs. He said: So two pairs will be in Paradise and one pair will be in Hellfire. He said: The one who is foremost is the one who is… Knowledge is often for desire, and the other: the one whom God has sealed with knowledge prevailing over desire, these two are a pair in Paradise, and the other: his desire is overpowering his knowledge, so this is the pair in Hell. The Arab scholars differed about the subject of the verb the companions of the right and the companions of the left.

x: Some of the grammarians of Basra said: The predicate of his statement, So the companions of the right is
What are the companions of the right
? and the companions of the left is What are the companions of the left? He said: And Zaid says: How strong Zaid is.”
What are the companions of the right

? The sentence is not its predicate, but the second refers back to the first and is an expression of astonishment. So it is as if he said: Who are the companions of the right? What is the calamity? What is the inevitable? So the dual refers back to the first and is an expression of astonishment. Astonishment has the meaning of predicate. If it were an interrogative, it would not be permissible for it to be predicate of the subject because an interrogative cannot be a predicate and a predicate cannot be an interrogative, and astonishment can be a predicate, so it was predicate of the subject. His statement, Zaid and what Zaid can only be from two statements because the letter and does not enter into the predicate of the subject, as if he said: This is Zaid and what is he? Meaning: How strong he is and how knowledgeable he is.
The people of interpretation differed regarding the two meanings of his statement,
Some of them said: They are those who prayed towards the two qiblas.

c: Ibn Hamid told us: Mihran told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Kharijah, on the authority of Qurrah, on the authority of Ibn Sirin:
m: h
And the foremost
are the foremost are those who prayed towards the two Qiblahs.

x: , means: In the orchards of eternal bliss.

God Almighty says: A group of past nations and a few from the nation of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, and they are the last. They were called the last because they are the last of the nations.

, some of which have been inserted into others, just as the rings of a shield are woven doubled over each other. From this comes the saying of Al-A'sha: And the fabric of David's loom is woven, and it is driven with the tribe, one by one. And from it is the lining of the camel, which is the lining of the belts if some of it is woven on top of the other in doubled order like the rings of the armor. It was said: Wadhin, but it is Mawdoon, inflected from Mafool to Fa’il, just as it was said: Qatil for Maqtool. It was reported that some Arabs heard the bricks placed one on top of the other, meaning a weak mashraj. It was said that it has decorated beds because it is woven with gold and jewels.

c: Ibn Bashar told us: Mu’ail told us: Sufyan told us: Hisin told us on the authority of Mujahid on the authority of Ibn Abbas:
m: h
On adorned couches
. He said: Decorated with gold.
b.via: Mujahid on the authority of Ibn Abbas

c: Ibn Hamid told us: Mihran told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Al-Hussain, on the authority of Mujahid:
m: h
On adorned couches
. He said: adorned with gold.

c: Muhammad bin Saad told me: My father told me: My uncle told me: My father told me on the authority of his father on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: regarding his statement,
h
On lined couches
, he said: He means the lined couches.
b.via: his father on the authority of Ibn Abbas

c: Hanad told us: Abu Al-Ahwas told us, on the authority of Hisin, on the authority of Mujahid, who said:
m: Al-Mawduna is the one covered with gold.

c: Ibn Hamid told us: Yahya bin Wadh told us: Al-Hussein bin Waqid told us, on the authority of Yazid, on the authority of Ikrimah,
m: regarding his statement,
h
On adorned couches
, he said: adorned with pearls and rubies.

c: Muhammad bin Amr told me: Abu Asim told us: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me: Al-Hasan told us: Warqa’ told us,
m: both on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement, adorned, he said: adorned with gold.

c: Bishr told us: Yazid told us: Saeed told us on the authority of Qatada
m: regarding his statement,
h
On lined couches
. The lined one is the one that is lined, and it is the softest of couches.

c: Ibn Bashar told us: Sulayman told us: Abu Hilal told us on the authority of Qatada
m: regarding his statement,
h
On lined couches
, he said: A woven sand couch.

c: It was narrated on the authority of Al-Hussein,
m: who said: I heard Abu Muadh say: Ubaid told us: I heard Al-Dahhak say regarding His statement,
h
On woven couches
, “Waddin” means interlacing and weaving. He said: Its middle is a woven mesh.

c: Yunus told me: Ibn Wahb told us: Ibn Zayd said
m: about His statement, On couches lined up, “lined up” means the one woven with leather. That is, the woven.

x: Others said: Rather, it means that it is arranged.

c: Ali told me: Abu Saleh told us: Muawiyah told us, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: regarding his statement,
h
on lined couches
, meaning: arranged in rows.

x: , facing each other, God Almighty says: Reclining on lined couches, facing each other, not looking at the backs of one another.

c: Ibn Hamid also told us: Mihran told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: regarding his statement, On thrones facing each other, he said: One of them should not look at the back of his companion. He mentioned that in Abdullah’s reading it is,
h
Reclining on them
facing each other.

c: Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna told us: Muhammad ibn Jaʿfar told us, on the authority of Shuʿbah, on the authority of Abu Ishaq:
m: In the recitation of Abdullah, meaning Ibn Masʿud, it is:
h
reclining on them
, facing each other. We have explained this in other places and mentioned what is in it of the narration.

evidence.text: Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna told us: Muhammad ibn Jaʿfar told us, on the authority of Shuʿbah, on the authority of Abu Ishaq: In the recitation of Abdullah, meaning Ibn Masʿud, it is: reclining on them, facing each other.

x: There will circulate among them immortal youths
, God Almighty says: There will circulate among these forerunners whom God has brought near in the Gardens of Bliss, youths of the same age who do not change and do not die.

c: Muhammad bin Amr told me: Abu Asim told us: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me: Al-Hasan told us: Warqa’ told us,
m: both on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid: Immortal means they will not die.

x: Others said: He meant that they were covered with earrings and bracelets. What is more correct in this regard is the statement of those who said that its meaning is: that they do not change and do not die, because that is the most obvious of its two meanings. The Arabs say about a man who has grown old and has not combed his hair: he is immortal, but it is a verbal noun from immortality.

And his saying, with cups and pitchers. Cups is the plural of cup, which is a pitcher that has a wide head and does not have a trunk. And in a similar manner to what we said about that, the people of interpretation said: Who said that?

c: Muhammad bin Saad told me: My father told us: My uncle told us: My father told me on the authority of his father on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: regarding his statement, with cups, he said: The cups are the silver jugs.
b.via: his father on the authority of Ibn Abbas

c: Ibn Bashar told us: Sufyan told us, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of Mujahid:
m: With cups and pitchers. He said: A pitcher is something that has spouts, and cups have spouts.

c: Ibn Bashar told us: Abd al-Rahman told us: Sufyan told us, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of Mujahid, who said:
m: Cups do not have ears.

c: Yaqub told us: Ibn Ulayyah told us on the authority of Abu Raja’
m: who said: Al-Hasan was asked about cups. He said: They are the pitchers from which water is poured for them.

c: Abu Kurayb and Abu al-Sa’ib told us: Ibn Idris told us:
m: I heard my father say: Abu Salih, the companion of al-Kalbi, passed by. My father said: Al-Hasan said to me while I was sitting, Ask him. I said: What are cups? He said: Silver jugs with round mouths and pitchers with spouts.

c: Ibn Hamid told us: Mihran told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of Mujahid:
m: With cups. He said: It has no handles or ears.

c: Bishr told us: Yazid told us: Saeed told us on the authority of Qatada
m: regarding his statement, with cups and pitchers. The cups from which water is scooped do not have spouts and are smaller than pitchers.

c: Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement, with cups and pitchers, he said: The cups that are smaller than pitchers do not have handles.

c: It was narrated on the authority of Al-Hussein,
m: who said: I heard Abu Muadh say: Ubaid told us, who said: I heard Al-Dahhak say: The cups are jars that do not have handles, and in Nabataean they are kubah, and it was narrated to me by Al-A’sha, who said: A delicious, creamy dish with a hint of butter between its cup and ear As for the jugs: they are the ones that have handles. His saying, And a cup of flowing water, and a cup of wine from a flowing drink that is apparent to the eyes. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.

c: Ali told me: Abu Saleh told us: Muawiyah told us, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: regarding his statement,
h
And a cup of pure wine
, he said: Wine.

c: Bishr told us: Yazid told us: Saeed told us on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement,
h
And a cup of flowing wine
, meaning of running wine.

c: It was narrated on the authority of Al-Hussein,
m: who said: I heard Abu Muadh say: Ubaid told us: I heard Al-Dahhak say regarding His statement, And a cup from a flowing spring, the cup means wine.

c: Abu Sinan told us: Sulayman told us: Abu Hilal told us on the authority of Qatada
m: regarding his statement,
h
And a cup of flowing wine
, he said: Running wine.

c: Ibn Hamid told us: Mihran told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Salamah ibn Nabit, on the authority of Ad-Dahhak,
m: similarly. His saying, They will not get a headache from it, means: Their heads will not get a headache from drinking it and thus become intoxicated. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.

c: Ismail bin Musa Al-Suddi told me: Sharik told us on the authority of Salim on the authority of Saeed,
m: regarding his statement,
h
They will not have a headache from it
, he said: Their heads will not be headaches.
b.via: Salim on the authority of Saeed

c: Bishr told us: Yazid told us: Saeed told us on the authority of Qatada:
m: They do not suffer a headache from it means it does not cause a headache.

c: Ibn Bashar told us: Sulayman told us: Abu Hilal told us on the authority of Qatada:
m: h
They will not have a headache from it
. He said: Their heads will not be broken.

c: Ibn Hamid told us: Mihran told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Mansour, on the authority of Mujahid:
m: h
They will not have a headache from it
. He said: Their heads will not be broken.

c: It was narrated on the authority of Al-Hussein,
m: who said: I heard Abu Muadh say: Ubaid narrated to us, who said: I heard Al-Dahhak say regarding His statement, They will not suffer a headache from it, meaning: a headache. And his saying, nor do they bleed. The reciters differed in its reading. The majority of the reciters of Medina and Basra read it nor do they bleed with a fat-ha on the zay, and they explained that by saying that their minds will not bleed. The majority of the reciters of Kufa read it nor do they bleed with a kasra on the zay, meaning: nor will their drink run out. The correct thing to say about this, in my opinion, is that they are two well-known readings with correct meanings, so whichever one the reader recites, he is correct.

x: The people of interpretation differed in their interpretation of this in the same way that the reciters differed in it. We mentioned the difference in their statements in this and explained the correct statement in Surat as-Saffat, so that made it unnecessary to repeat it in this place. However, I will remember the statement of some of them in this place so that no one will think that its meaning in this place is different from its meaning there.
Some of them said: It means do not let their minds bleed.

c: Ismail bin Musa told us: Sharik told us on the authority of Salim on the authority of Sa’id:
m: And they do not lose their minds. He said: Their minds do not lose their minds.
b.via: Salim on the authority of Sa’id

c: Ibn Hamid told us: Mihran told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Mansour, on the authority of Mujahid:
m: And they do not lose their minds. He said: Their minds do not lose their minds.

c: Ibn Hamid told us
m: again and said: Their minds will not go away.

c: It was narrated on the authority of Al-Hussein,
m: who said: I heard Abu Muadh say: Ubaid told us, who said: I heard Al-Dahhak say regarding His statement, nor will they be exhausted, that their minds will not be exhausted.

c: Bishr told us: Yazid told us, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement, nor shall they be overcome by insanity, he said: No one shall be overcome by his mind.

c: Ibn Bashar told us: Yazid told us: Saeed told us
m: regarding his statement, nor shall they be overcome by blood, they said: No one shall lose his mind.

c: Ibn Bashar told us: Sulayman told us: Abu Hilal told us on the authority of Qatada
m: regarding the statement of God, nor shall they be overcome by blood, he said: Their minds shall not be overcome.

evidence.text: The reciters differed in its reading.
The majority of the reciters of Medina and Basra read it nor do they bleed with a fat-ha on the zay, and they explained that by saying that their minds will not bleed.
The majority of the reciters of Kufa read it nor do they bleed with a kasra on the zay, meaning: nor will their drink run out.
The people of interpretation differed in their interpretation of this in the same way that the reciters differed in it.

The reciters differed in their recitation of His statement,
. The majority of the reciters of Kufa and some of the Medinans recited it as

in the accusative case, following its parsing like the parsing of what preceded it of fruit and meat, even though that is not something that is circumambulated. But since its intended meaning was known, the latter followed the former in parsing, as some poets said: If the prostitutes appear one day and raise their eyebrows and eyes The eyes are lined with kohl, but only the eyebrows are lined. So, in parsing, it is returned to the eyebrows so that the listener will understand the meaning of that, as the other said: You hear a rumbling sound from his entrails, and a grinding sound from his hands. Al-Jasah: roughness in the hand that does not hear.

Some of the readers of Medina and Mecca and some of the people of Basra read it in the nominative case, and houris of wide-eyed women, as a subject, and they said: The houris of wide-eyed women are not to be walked around with, so it is permissible to connect them in the syntactic sense to fruit and meat, but it is in the nominative case, meaning: and with them are houris of wide-eyed women, or they have houris of wide-eyed women. The correct thing to say about this, in my opinion, is: They are two well-known readings, each of which has been read by a group of readers, despite their meanings being close. So whichever of the two readings the reader reads, he is correct. Al-Hoor is a group of Hawra’, which is the pure whiteness of the eye and its intense blackness. Al-Ayn is the plural of ‘Ayna’, which is the clear, beautiful eye.

From this comes the saying of Al-A’sha: If he punishes with a fine or gives generously, he does not care. What he means by his saying: It will be a loss is: It will be a torment. In the speech, I will suffice with the indication of the speech to it, which is: So you kept joking, saying, We are indeed in love. Why do you not give thanks
Why do you not give thanks
to your Lord for giving you what He gave you of fresh water for your drinking, your benefits, and the improvement of your lives, and leaving it brackish so that you do not benefit from it?

God Almighty says: Have you seen, O people, the fire that you extract from your own firewood? Did you create its tree? He says: Did you create its tree and invent its origin? They said: O Prophet of God, is that sufficient? He said: It has been struck with water two or two times so that the children of Adam may benefit from it and come near to it.

c: Ibn Hamid told us: Mihran told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Jabir, on the authority of Mujahid,

The most correct of the sayings in this regard, in my opinion, is the saying of the one who said: What is meant by this is the traveler who has no provisions with him or anything for himself, and its origin is from their saying: The sustenance of the house: if it is empty of its people and inhabitants, as the poet said: Stronger and more desolate than Na'am and others, the raging wind that blows away the dust He means by his saying stronger than its inhabitants. m: regarding his statement,

So I swear by the positions of the stars

, he said: Al-Hasan said, their setting and scattering on the Day of Resurrection. The most correct of the sayings on this matter is the saying of those who said: The meaning of that is: I do not swear by the places where the stars fall and set in the sky. This is because mawaqe’ is the plural of mawaqe’ and mawaqe’ is the verbal noun from waqa’a, which means waq’a, so the most common of its meanings and the most apparent of its interpretations is what we said on this matter. Therefore we said: This is the most deserving of its meanings. The readers differed in reading this. The majority of the readers of Kufa read it in a position on the unification, and the majority of the readers of Medina and Basra and some of the Kufians read it in positions: on the group. The correct thing to say about this is that they are two well-known readings with one meaning, so whichever one the reader reads, he is correct. So glorify the name of your Lord, the Great.

with God, and nothing of harm, such as dust or anything else, touches it. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.

None shall touch it except the purified

Is it this narration that you are doubting
? He said: Are you lying and not believing?
b.via: his father on the authority of Ibn Abbas

m: who said: I heard Abu Muadh say: Ubaid told us, who said: I heard Al-Dahhak say regarding His statement, You are deceivers, meaning: liars.

, means: And you make thanking God for His provision to you a lie. m: I think it was him or someone else. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, heard a man say when it rained: We were rained upon by some of the lion’s cubs. He said: “You have lied. Rather, it is God’s provision.”

c: Yunus told me, he said: Sufyan told us, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Ishaq, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Ibrahim ibn al-Harith al-Taymi, on the authority of Abu Salamah, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah,
m: that the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: Verily, God may bless a people in the morning or in the evening, and a people may become disbelievers in the morning because of it, ‘We have been given rain by the star of such and such.’ Muhammad said: “So I mentioned the blessing or He may bless them in the evening, and a people may become disbelievers in the morning because of it, and they say, ‘We have been given rain by the star of such and such.’” Muhammad said: “So I mentioned this hadith to Sa’id ibn al-Musayyab, and he said: We have heard it from Abu Hurayrah, and someone told me that he witnessed Umar ibn al-Khattab may God be pleased with him praying for rain. When he prayed for rain, he turned to al-Abbas and said: ‘O Abbas, O uncle of the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him), how much of the Pleiades star remains?’ He said: ‘The scholars of it claim that it appears on the horizon seven times after its setting.’ He said: ‘Not even seven days had passed before they had rain.’”

c: Ibn Hamid told us: Mihran told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Abd al-A’la, on the authority of Abu Abd al-Rahman, on the authority of Ali:
m: h
And you make your provision that you lie

. He said: He used to recite it: And you make your gratitude that you lie. He said: You made God’s provision in the stars’ stars, and their provision was in themselves in the stars, the stars of rain. When rain came to them, they said, We were provided with such-and-such a star. But when it was withheld from them, they lied. So that was their denial.
Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Ata’

evidence.text: He said: He used to recite it: And you make your gratitude that you lie.

x: And His statement, Why, then, when it reaches the throat? God Almighty says: Why, then, when the souls, O people, reach your throats, and you at that time are looking on? He says: And whoever of your family is present at them at that time is looking at them. The address here is general to everyone, and what is meant by it is whoever of the family of the deceased is present and others. This is well-known from the speech of the Arabs, which is that a group is addressed by the verb as if they were his family and companions, and what is meant by it is some of them, whether they are absent or present, so he says, You killed so-and-so, and the killer is one of them, either absent or present. We have explained similar examples of this in many places in this book of ours.
And you will then be watching.
He says, And We are nearer to him than you. He says, And Our messengers who take his soul are nearer to him than you, but you do not see.

Some of the Arab scholars from Basra used to say: It was said, Why, when it reaches the throat, and you are then looking on? It was as if he had heard from them, and God knows best, that we are able not to die. So he said, Why, when it reaches the throat? Then he said, Why, if you are not to be held accountable? That is, not to be able to compensate those souls, and you see how they will come out at that time, if you are truthful in that you are preventing death.
God Almighty says: Why then, O people, if you were not indebted?
The people of interpretation differed regarding his statement, debted.
Some of them said, not accountable.

c: Ali told me: Abu Saleh told us: Muawiyah told us on the authority of Ali on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: regarding his statement, Then why, if you were not to be held accountable, he means not to be held accountable.

c: Muhammad bin Amr told me: Abu Asim told us: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me: Al-Hasan told us: Warqa’ told us,
m: both on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement, not being held accountable, he said, not being held accountable.

c: Bishr told us: Yazid told us: Saeed told us on the authority of Qatada:
m: Why, if you were not to be judged, he said: They denied that they would be judged after death. He said: And He is the Master of the Day of Judgment, the day when people will be judged for their deeds. He said: They will be judged: they will be held accountable.

c: Yaqub told me: Ibn Ulayyah told us: Abu Raja’ told us on the authority of Al-Hasan
m: regarding his statement, Then why, if you were not to be held accountable, he said, not to be held accountable.

c: Ibn Bashar told us: Sulayman told us: Abu Hilal told us on the authority of Qatada:
m: Why, if you were not to be judged? He said: Not resurrected and not held accountable.

x: Others said that it means not being sent.

c: Ibn Bashar told us, he said: Hudha told us, he said: Aouf told us, on the authority of Al-Hasan:
m: Then why, if you are not to be recompensed - not to be resurrected on the Day of Resurrection, you will return it if you are truthful.

x: Others said: Rather, it means that you are not rewarded for your deeds. The most correct of the sayings on this matter is the saying of those who said: They will not be held accountable, but will be rewarded for your deeds, based on their saying, As you judge, you will be judged, and on the saying of God, Owner of the Day of Judgment (al-Fatihah 1:4).

, if you are truthful, means: You will return those souls after their destination is the throats to their final resting place in the bodies, if you are truthful, if you are abstaining from death, accountability, and recompense. The answer to His statement, Then why, when it reaches the throat, and the answer to His statement, Then why, if you are not to be held accountable, is one answer, which is His statement,

, and that is similar to His statement, But if there comes to you guidance from Me, then whoever follows My guidance will have no fear (al-Baqarah 2:38). He made the answer to the two recompenses one answer. And in a similar manner to what we said about His statement,

m: regarding His statement,

, He said to that soul, If you are truthful.

x: And His statement, But if he was among those brought near, * then there is comfort and fragrance. God Almighty says: But if the deceased was among those brought near whom God brought near to be near Him in His Paradise, then there is comfort and fragrance. He says, He has comfort and fragrance. The reciters differed in reading this. The majority of reciters in the regions read it as farooh with a fatha on the ra’, meaning he has coolness, and basil meaning and abundant provision according to some of them, and according to others he has comfort and basil. Al-Hasan al-Basri read it as farooh with a damma on the ra’, meaning that his soul comes out in basil. The first of the two readings is the correct one, which reads it with the fat-ha, due to the consensus of the authoritative reciters on it, meaning: For Him is mercy, forgiveness, and good and pleasant provision. The commentators differed in their interpretation of his statement, A place of rest and relaxation.
Some of them said: It means comfort and rest.

c: Ali told me: Abu Saleh told us: Muawiyah told us, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas:
m: Farooh and basil means comfort and rest.

c: Muhammad bin Saad told me: My father told me: My uncle told me: My father told me on the authority of his father on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: regarding his statement, But if he is of those brought near, * There will be comfort and basil. He said, Blessings means the one who is relieved from this world. And a Garden of Delights means forgiveness and mercy.

m: both on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement, And rest and fragrance, he said: Rest. And his statement, And fragrance, he said: Provision.

x: Others said: The spirit means joy and basil means sustenance.

m: I heard my father, on the authority of Abu Ishaq, on the authority of Saeed Ibn Jubayr, regarding his statement, And comfort and basil, he said: Comfort means joy and basil means provision. As for those who read it with a damma on the ra’, they said: The soul is the soul of the human being and the basil is the well-known basil. They said that the meaning of this is that the souls of those close to God leave their bodies at death with basil that you smell.

c: Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Al-Mu’tamir told us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of al-Hasan:
m: Farooh and basil. He said: His soul comes out in his basil.

m: he heard Abu Muadh say: Ubaid told us that he heard Al-Dahhak say: Farooh and basil. The spirit means forgiveness and mercy, and basil means rest.

c: Ibn Bashar told us: Hammad told us: Qurra told us on the authority of Al-Hasan,
m: with a similar narration. The most correct of the sayings in this regard, in my opinion, is the saying of the one who said about me by the spirit: joy, mercy, and forgiveness. Its origin is from their saying: I found a spirit, if he found a breeze to which he could breathe from the distress of the heat. As for basil, in my opinion it is the basil that is received at death, as Abu al-Aaliyah and al-Hasan said, and whoever said something similar to their saying, because that is the most common and most apparent

of its meanings. And his saying, And a garden of pleasures, means: He also has a garden of pleasures in which he can enjoy himself.

m: A paradise of bliss. He said: It was shown to him.

Others said, among them is his statement, But if he is among those brought near, for he combined two answers to show that but is a reward. He said: As for his statement, “
Then peace be upon you from the companions of the right
,” he said: This is the root of the word, This is Muslim to you, then that was deleted and from was used in its place. He said: It has been said: “

, you are among the companions of the right,” so it is like that: meaning, peace be upon you. It is said: You are among the companions of the right, and all of this is based on two statements. He said: It has been said: Muslim, meaning just as you say: “

from the people,” just as you say: Then a drink for you from the people, so it becomes one statement. The most correct of the sayings on this matter is to say: Its meaning is: Peace be upon you, for you are among the companions of the right hand.
Then he omitted and dared to indicate that it was on her, so you were saved from the punishment of God and from what you dislike because you are among the companions of the right hand.
"Peace be upon you from the companions of the right hand."

And His statement, But if he was among the deniers and the astray, * then he will be given scalding water. God Almighty says: But if the deceased was among those who denied the signs of God and deviated from His path, then he will be given scalding water that has been boiled until its heat reaches its utmost limit, and that is his drink.
Then he sent down scalding water.

And the burning of Hellfire He says: And the burning of Hellfire with which he burns. And the burning is the active participle from the prayer of God to the Fire, so he burns him with a burning, and that is if he burns him with it.

God Almighty says: Indeed, what I have informed you of, O people, regarding the report of those brought near to God, the companions of the right hand, and the deniers who have gone astray, and what their affairs will eventually lead to, is the certain truth. He says: It is the certain truth of the report, there is no doubt about it. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.

c: Muhammad bin Amr told me: Abu Asim told us: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me: Al-Hasan told us: Warqa’ told us,
m: both on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid: Indeed, this is the certain truth. He said: The certain report.

c: Bishr told us: Yazid told us: Saeed told us on the authority of Qatada:
m: “But if he is among the deniers and the astray, then he will be sent with scalding water and will be burned in Hellfire. Indeed, this is the certainty of truth.” Until he concluded: God Almighty will not leave anyone of His creation until He makes him stand on certainty of this Qur’an. As for the believer, he is certain in this world, and that will benefit him on the Day of Resurrection. As for the disbeliever, he is certain on the Day of Resurrection when it will not benefit him. The Arab scholars differed about the reason for adding the truth to certainty, and the truth is certainty.

x: Some of the grammarians of Basra said: He said: The truth of certainty, so he added the truth to certainty, just as he said, That is the upright religion Al-Bayyinah 5, meaning that is the religion of the upright religion, and that is the truth of the certain matter. He said: As for this evil man, there is no evil in this man as there is in the truth of certainty, because the black man is not the man, and certainty is the truth.

Some of the people of Kufa said: Certainty is an attribute of the truth, as if he said: The truth is certainty and the upright religion, and something similar has come in many speeches and the Qur’an, And for the home of the Hereafter Yusuf 109 - An-Nahl 30, And for the home of the Hereafter Al-A’raf 169 - Al-Ahzab 29. He said: So if it is added, something other than the first is imagined.
So glorify the name of your Lord
, the Most Great, God Almighty says:
So glorify the name of your Lord
, the Most Great, with His beautiful names.
Commentary on Sūrat The Event (al-Wāqiʿah). In the name of God, the Most Compassionate, the Most Merciful.
